newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus Popular '96 pre-tax profit up 6.2pct.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus Popular '96 pre-tax profit up 6.2pct.

text.p: The Cyprus Popular Bank Group on Friday announced a 6.20 percent rise in its preliminary 1996 pre-tax profits, after a 17.5 percent increase the year before.

"The (island's) economy in 1996 did not go so well. The environment which prevailed was restrictive and this of course affected the activities of the commercial banks. In that framework the results of the group are satisfactory," bank Chief Executive and Chairman Kikis Lazarides told a news conference.
Pre-tax profit of the group for 1996 reached 27.641 million pounds ($54.5 million) from 26.027 in 1995, Lazarides said. He announced a 20 percent dividend to shareholders, the same as last year.
Operating profit for 1996 reached 36.754 million pounds, up 11.11 percent from 1995, while net profit increased by 5.78 percent to 19.424 million pounds.
"Developments were more favourable abroad than at home, and the contribution of overseas to operating profit went up considerably to 16 percent from 10 percent in 1995," Lazarides said.

A slowdown in transactions on the Cyprus Stock Exchange (CSE) had a significant impact on business of Laiki Investments, the brokerage subsidiary of the bank. Compensation for damages after an earthquake in October last year had an impact on the profits of subsidiary Laiki Insurance, he added.

The Popular Bank operates in Greece and Britain, with representative offices in Australia, South Africa and Canada. The Hong Kong and Shanghai Bank (HSBC) owns 22 percent of the Cyprus Popular Bank. ($=0.506 pounds)
